task.description: Gate lib/letflow/design/iss0444-poller-schema-availability.md before ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-DESIGNER proceed: verify rescue-boundary placement, precedent citations, poll_result() decision, retention-sweep scope decision, and absence of implementation code, each against source directly rather than trusting the design doc's own summary.

result.summary:
Six of seven checks pass on independent verification. One factual inaccuracy found in §4's justification for NOT rescuing inside EventStore.archive/1, sufficient to fail this gate.

1. RESCUE BOUNDARY (claim_due_timer_ids/2): CONFIRMED. Read scheduler.ex:191-235 directly. poll_and_fire/1's @doc literally says 'Never raises -- every per-timer failure is caught internally and folded into the returned counts (design §2.2, §2.5)' (scheduler.ex:185-190) and its body's first statement is the unguarded claim_due_timer_ids(tenant_schema, max_timers_per_cycle()) call (line 193). claim_due_timer_ids/2's body (lines 222-235) is exactly one Repo.all(query, prefix: tenant_schema) call with zero try/rescue, matching the design's characterization precisely.

2. poller.ex MODULEDOC QUOTE: CONFIRMED verbatim. poller.ex:30-35 reads exactly as the design doc quotes it at §0: 'A raise inside one tenant schema's Letflow.Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1 call is not additionally guarded here -- that function's own contract (design §2.2) already guarantees it never raises, so a second, redundant try/rescue around the Enum.each below would duplicate an already-established isolation boundary for no additional safety property.' The design's paraphrase is not a paraphrase at all -- it is the literal text.

3. PIN_REBIND.EX:372-390 PRECEDENT: CONFIRMED. lock_projection_nowait/2 (pin_rebind.ex:376-393) has exactly the shape claimed: rescue error in Postgrex.Error ->, then if match?(%Postgrex.Error{postgres: %{code: :lock_not_available}}, error) -> {:error, ...}; else -> reraise error, __STACKTRACE__ end. Narrow, single-code match, re-raise-else -- the design's central idiom justification for §1's rescue shape holds up exactly as cited.

4. scheduler_test.exs:578-579: CONFIRMED. Lines read: 'assert length(Scheduler.claim_due_timer_ids(schema_name, 3)) == 3' and 'assert length(Scheduler.claim_due_timer_ids(schema_name, 2)) == 2' -- both call length/1 against the return value, unaffected by an unchanged [Ecto.UUID.t()] return type. Design's claim that this assertion pair is untouched is accurate.

5. LOGGER PRECEDENTS: CONFIRMED both citations, and the alerts.ex-over-backfill.ex choice is accurately described. backfill.ex:44-48 uses Logger.warning/1 with a SINGLE interpolated string argument only, no keyword metadata -- confirmed. alerts.ex:588-592 uses Logger.warning/2 with message string + keyword list ('component:'/'ref:') -- confirmed. poller.ex's own with_admission/3 (poller.ex:174-177, this same REQ-218 cycle) already independently chose the alerts.ex shape (schema:/op: keys) for an analogous schema-plus-context skip log -- the design's 'closer, more local, already-established-in-a-sibling-function-in-this-same-file precedent' reasoning for choosing alerts.ex's shape over backfill.ex's for THIS fix is sound and accurately sourced.

6. poll_result()/[]-RETURN SAFETY TRACE: CONFIRMED, no downstream misinference risk. poll_and_fire/1 (scheduler.ex:192-213) does Enum.reduce(timer_ids, %{... claimed: length(timer_ids), ...}, fn ...) -- for timer_ids = [], Enum.reduce short-circuits to the initial accumulator unchanged, i.e. the all-zero poll_result() map, which is exactly what a legitimately-empty poll already produces today. This is not a new code path, only an existing one reached for an additional reason. Grepped scheduler.ex and poller.ex for any branch inspecting claimed/fired/errored/exhausted == 0 to make a further inference (e.g. alerting, backoff, retry escalation) -- none found; the only occurrences of 'claimed' are the @type field declaration (scheduler.ex:179) and its one assignment (scheduler.ex:199). No caller of poll_and_fire/1 (Poller.handle_info/2, poller.ex:131-135) inspects the returned map's fields at all -- its result is discarded inside Enum.each. Confirms the design's claim that collapsing 'schema unavailable' into the existing all-zero shape carries no observable behavioral risk beyond the intended Logger line.

7. NO IMPLEMENTATION CODE: CONFIRMED independently. `grep -n '```' lib/letflow/design/iss0444-poller-schema-availability.md` returned zero hits; `grep -nE '^\s*(def|defp)\s' ...` also returned zero hits. CODE-DESIGNER's own claim to have caught and removed all code fences/def bodies during drafting is verified true, not merely trusted.

8. RETENTION-SWEEP SCOPE JUDGMENT (independent agreement, separate from the factual defect below): AGREE with including run_retention_sweep/1's identical fix in this same design rather than filing a separate issue. run_retention_sweep/1 (scheduler.ex:564-566) is confirmed to be a one-line delegation with an @spec already including {:error, term()} (scheduler.ex, immediately preceding lines) -- zero type-shape change needed, and the fix is a mechanical reuse of the SAME rescue clause shape already designed for §1, not an independent second design decision. The 'defect already fully traced, fixing costs no more than describing it' basis is sound specifically because both call sites share one root cause, one rescue shape, and one log shape -- this is not the kind of scope creep that changes what ORCH scoped this workflow to do (still 'fix ISS-0444's poll_and_fire never-raises gap'), it is completing the same fix for a second call site the diagnosis step itself already surfaced as the identical defect class.

--- FACTUAL DISCREPANCY (fails the gate) ---

§4's justification for placing the retention-sweep rescue in Scheduler.run_retention_sweep/1 rather than inside EventStore.archive/1 asserts: 'archive/1 is a general-purpose context function with several OTHER callers/contexts implied by its own moduledoc (per-event-type retention policies, idempotent re-invocation).' This is INACCURATE as stated. Grepped the whole lib/ and test/ tree for 'EventStore.archive(': the ONLY production call site anywhere in lib/ is lib/letflow/scheduler.ex:565 (run_retention_sweep/1 itself) -- there are no other production callers. The only other call sites are direct test invocations (test/letflow/event_store_test.exs and test/letflow/engine/reconstruction_test.exs), which are unit tests exercising archive/1 in isolation, not 'other contexts' in the runtime/production sense the design's wording implies. (The unrelated grep hits for 'Definitions.archive(' are a completely different function on Letflow.Definitions, not EventStore.archive/1 -- not relevant.) EventStore.archive/1's own moduledoc (event_store.ex:980-999) documents per-event-type retention-policy precedence and idempotency as PROPERTIES of what archive/1 does, not as evidence of multiple callers or contexts -- the design doc conflates these two different things. The design's underlying instinct (don't widen a general-purpose EventStore function's rescue behavior just to fix one caller) may still be the right call, but the STATED reason ('several OTHER callers/contexts') is not true today and cannot be used as-is to justify it -- a future CODE-DESIGNER, REVIEWER, or ELIXIR-DEV reading this design as the source of truth would be relying on a fabricated fact.
result.rework_instructions: Correct §4's justification for NOT placing the rescue inside EventStore.archive/1. Do not claim 'archive/1 has several OTHER callers/contexts' -- grep confirms its only production caller is Letflow.Scheduler.run_retention_sweep/1 itself (the function this design already fixes); its only OTHER call sites are direct unit-test invocations in test/letflow/event_store_test.exs and test/letflow/engine/reconstruction_test.exs. Replace the justification with an accurate one -- for example: (a) archive/1 is directly exercised by ~10 existing test call sites that assert specific {:ok,...}/{:error,...} return shapes for scenarios that assume a physically-present schema; widening archive/1's own rescue behavior would need to be checked against every one of those for behavioral change, which is a larger and less-scoped verification burden than adding one rescue clause to the one function (run_retention_sweep/1) that Poller's own retention path actually reaches; and/or (b) archive/1 is EventStore's general-purpose primitive by design intent (its moduledoc documents retention-policy precedence and idempotency as reusable properties for future callers beyond today's single one), so keeping schema-availability handling out of it preserves that generality for whatever calls it next, rather than baking one caller's (Scheduler's) specific recovery behavior into the shared primitive. Pick whichever of these (or another equally accurate justification) the design actually intends, cite the grep evidence (or your own re-verification of it) explicitly, and do not restate 'several OTHER callers' as a present-tense fact. No other section requires changes -- §1, §2, §3, and the rest of §4 (rescue shape, placement inside run_retention_sweep/1 itself, {:error, {:schema_unavailable, tenant_schema}} reason-term choice, no second issue filed) all verified accurate and require no rework.

checks.archive1_other_callers_claim: FAIL -- factually inaccurate, only production caller is run_retention_sweep/1 itself
